chunks: Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from al-Qāsim ibn ʿUrwah, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurārah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

For the hand, there is half of the diyah, and for both hands together, the full diyah. And for both legs likewise. And for the male organ, if the glans and what is above that are cut, then the diyah is due. And for the nose, if the soft part is cut, the diyah is due.

key_terms.نِصْفُ ٱلدِّيَةِ: half of the full legal compensation
key_terms.ٱلدِّيَةِ: blood money or legal financial compensation for bodily injury
key_terms.ٱلْحَشَفَةُ: the glans of the male organ
key_terms.ٱلْمَارِنُ: the soft projecting part of the nose

ai.seo_question: What bodily injuries require full or half diyah in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states specific fiqh rulings for bodily injuries that incur full or half diyah. It identifies the compensation due for injury to a hand, both hands, both legs, the male organ when the glans and beyond are cut, and the nose when its soft part is cut.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5285 - Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Al-Qasim ibn Urwah from Ibn Bukayr from Zurara from Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) who said:

"For the hand, there is half of the full blood money (diyya), and for both hands together, the full diyya is due. Similarly, for both legs, the full diyya applies.
For the male organ, if the glans (Al-hashafa) and above it are cut off, the full diyya is required.
For the nose, if the soft part (Al-marin) is cut off, the full diyya applies."
